paths.description: Homepage/live-score listing, primary public journey and global chrome. Represents sport listing templates.
Europa League competition page, representing league/standings/result listings.
Completed Qarabag v CSKA Sofia match detail, representing event timelines and odds/detail tabs.
Sports news index, representing editorial listing surfaces.
Invalid route used to test failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: Theme does not follow the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are visually identical, and the loaded CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule. The page imposes its dark theme rather than adapting to the system setting.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Infinite shimmer animation continues under reduced motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion evaluate probe reported the same 13 running placeholderShimmer animations, each 1500ms with infinite iterations, as the normal condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable shimmer and other non-essential looping animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures the primary scores on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show the privacy dialog covering the entire content area on load. On mobile, the live-score task is pushed completely out of the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface where legally possible, preserve equal Accept/Reject choices, and keep primary content visible.

findings.summary: Consent overlays are custom role=dialog divs rather than native dialogs.
findings.evidence: The recon probe found two [role=dialog] DIV elements and zero native dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the modal consent flow with native focus containment and close semantics.

findings.summary: Gambling promotions dominate the mobile first viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, three brightly colored betting cards and an Advertisement label occupy the main area above score filters, before any match content.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or collapse promotional modules below the core scores, reserve the first viewport for the primary task, and cap ad density.

findings.summary: Several navigation targets are only 16px high.
findings.evidence: The interaction probe measured at least eight visible league links at 16 CSS px high, below the recommended target size, although keyboard focus itself had a visible 2px outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand the interactive hit area to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls, without changing compact visual density.

findings.summary: Initial load is slow and main-thread heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 13.5s, TBT 1,070ms, Speed Index 9.8s and performance 0.33. The first-party trace corroborated LCP 4.91s and six long tasks with 129.54ms TBT in a separate run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, defer non-critical scripts and promotions, and break long tasks into scheduler-yielding chunks.

findings.summary: The critical path carries excessive requests and render-blocking CSS.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 237 requests and 2.75MB transferred, including 50 scripts and 39 stylesheets; its grounded candidate list contains at least ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, confirmed by the document DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle and inline only critical CSS, load route-specific styles on demand, and defer low-value scripts and ad dependencies.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JavaScript and CSS ship on the home route.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 677 KiB unused JavaScript and 82 KiB unused CSS; liveTable.js was 73% unused and several route/header bundles were over 80% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and interaction, remove duplicate analytics destinations, and load live-table and login code only when needed.

findings.summary: Some focusable links have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two unnamed links, including a 14x14 TV event icon and the GambleAware logo; the DOM probe found five empty links without text, aria-label, or img alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each icon-only link a concise accessible name and ensure decorative links are removed from the tab order.

findings.summary: Heading order skips levels in news content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified an H3 news headline reached without a preceding H2 in the relevant content hierarchy.
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings to reflect the page outline rather than visual size, with section H2 headings before article H3 headings.

findings.summary: Dense mobile legal and advertising copy is difficult to read.
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshot shows long consent paragraphs and betting terms rendered at roughly 9 to 11px with tight line spacing, creating a dense wall of text.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase minimum text size and line-height for legal copy, constrain line length, and progressively disclose secondary terms without hiding required information.

findings.summary: The page throws an uncaught TypeError during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading getIdent) at the main document around line 2904.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the dependency before calling getIdent and add load-path error monitoring/regression coverage.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and one header image is distorted.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all 100 sampled images without width/height attributes; Lighthouse found header bg.png rendered at 8.58:1 despite a natural ratio of 12.48:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and use object-fit/cropping rather than distorting the header asset.

findings.summary: Some crawlable links have empty or generic text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO found a generic More information link and accessibility found unnamed href links; the recon probe also showed many match anchors with empty text.
findings.suggestedFix: Put descriptive text in each href anchor or provide an equivalent accessible name that identifies the destination.

findings.summary: Rich sports entities lack structured data.
findings.evidence: Home, league, news and match probes found accurate Open Graph metadata, but no JSON-LD. The match detail is a rich sporting event with teams, status and date that can be represented structurally.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org SportsEvent/Event JSON-LD to match pages and suitable CollectionPage/NewsArticle data to listing/article templates.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; the only observed consent cookie also lacked Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy and least-privilege permissions policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure.

findings.summary: The page loads a broad tracking and third-party footprint before consent.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 10 third-party origins and Google Ads, Tag Manager and Analytics. HAR attributed 225/237 requests and 2.63MB to third-party origins; the consent UI states 1001 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential tags until affirmative consent, consolidate analytics, remove redundant ad destinations, and minimize partner/vendor scope.

findings.summary: Image delivery relies almost entirely on legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The image primitive classified 99 of 100 images as legacy PNG/GIF and only one as modern; all sampled images lacked intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where appropriate, retain SVG for logos, provide responsive sources, and preserve intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Background and third-party work is disproportionate to the core scores task.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.75MB and 237 requests, including more than 530KB from Google Tag Manager endpoints and large consent/ad payloads; Lighthouse found 677KiB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route budget, defer ads/analytics until idle and consented, eliminate duplicate tags, and fetch match modules only on demand.
